Q217.L1t: Tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon and, to a lesser extent, the Sun on Earth's oceans.
Q217.L2t: The Moon takes about 24 hours 50 minutes to return to the same position overhead, because it moves along its orbit while Earth rotates.
Q217.L3t: Most coasts get two high tides per lunar day, from tidal bulges on the near and far sides of Earth, so the gap between them is half of the roughly 24 hour 50 minute lunar day.
Q217.L4t: High tides come on average a little over twelve hours apart, about twelve and a quarter hours.
Q217.L2f: Tidal ranges are largest at neap tides, when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles to each other.
Q217.L3f: Each lunar day of about 24 hours 50 minutes contains roughly seven evenly spaced high tides, because the oceans form many bulges as Earth rotates.
Q217.L4f: The average gap between successive high tides is only a little over three hours.

Q266.L1t: Greenland is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, with a small population of about 56,000 people.
Q266.L2t: Greenland has long been reported to have one of the highest suicide rates in the world, especially among young Inuit men.
Q266.L3t: Greenland's suicide rate is about 60 per 100,000 people per year, while its overall death rate is roughly 850 per 100,000, so suicide makes up several percent of all deaths.
Q266.L4t: Suicide accounts for roughly one in fourteen deaths in Greenland, a little over seven percent.
Q266.L2f: Greenland's suicide rates are highest among elderly women, and young men are the group least affected.
Q266.L3f: Greenland's suicide rate is only about 8 per 100,000 per year, close to the European average, while its overall death rate is roughly 850 per 100,000.
Q266.L4f: Suicide accounts for less than one percent of all deaths in Greenland.

Q265.L1t: Economic growth is commonly measured as the percentage change in real average income per person over time.
Q265.L2t: Income growth in Britain during the industrial revolution was historically unprecedented but modest by modern standards, well under 2% per year.
Q265.L3t: Britain's average incomes grew at only about 1% per year during its industrial revolution, whereas less developed countries averaged around 2% per year over 1960 to 1995, roughly in line with the pace of rich countries.
Q265.L4t: Poorer countries' income growth over this period outpaced the rate Britain achieved during its industrial revolution.
Q265.L2f: Britain's industrial revolution began in the early twentieth century, after the First World War.
Q265.L3f: Between 1960 and 1995 average incomes in high income countries grew only about 1% per year, while less developed countries averaged around 4% per year.
Q265.L4f: Poorer countries' incomes grew faster than those of rich countries over this period, so they were catching up.
